t: D1 vs C5 (Luke 3:23): UNDERDETERMINED. The challenger argues "as was supposed" ([L1] Luke 3:23, [L2] enomizeto) labels the father-language as supposition, but the defender answers with Acts 16:13 ([L3]) where the same verb means "was wont," leaving the lexical weight of the qualifier unresolved.

D2 vs C6 (Galatians 4:4): UNDERDETERMINED. The challenger argues "made of a woman" ([L1] Galatians 4:4) names the only human source, but the defender answers that this is a mortality idiom applied even to those with named fathers ([L3] Job 14:1, Matthew 11:11), leaving the exclusion of a father unresolved.

D4 vs C4 (John 1:13): UNDERDETERMINED. The challenger argues John 1:13 ([L1]) sets "of God" against "the will of man," but the defender answers that this row describes regeneration of believers ([L3] 1 John 3:9), leaving the application to the conception unresolved.

D5 vs C7 (1 Chronicles 2:34): UNDERDETERMINED. The challenger argues 1 Chronicles 2:34-35 ([L1]) shows house reckoning differs from biology, but the defender answers that the text there explicitly names the begetter ("she bare him", [L1]), leaving whether a silent register implies biology unresolved.

D1 vs C4 (Luke 3:23): UNDERDETERMINED -- the naming registers and the words "as was supposed" were both answered from the text, and the unanswered examples of the supposing-verb do not state that the mother's "thy father" is false.
D2 vs C5 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- the flesh-seed rows and "made of a woman" were both answered, and no answered witness states that the seed came out of Joseph's body or that it did not.

D3 vs C1 (Matthew 1:25): UNDERDETERMINED -- "knew her not till she had brought forth" and the knowing-then-conceiving idiom were both answered, and together they still leave open whether the timing excludes a begetter.

D3 vs C3 (Luke 1:35): UNDERDETERMINED -- "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" and the "therefore" were answered as a title's ground by one side and as a mechanism by the other, and the words leave both readings open.

D4 vs C2 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" was answered both as covenant-origin language and as the only named source, and the parallels do not close which register this row uses.

D4 vs C3 (Luke 1:35): UNDERDETERMINED -- "the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee" was answered as empowerment and as the reply to a question about no man, and the context does not force one reading.

D5 vs C6 (1 Chronicles 2:35): UNDERDETERMINED -- "she bare him Attai" names the begetter and the line is reckoned in Sheshan's house, and both sides answered the row, so whether a house-register requires that father's seed stays open.

D6 vs C1 (Matthew 1:18): UNDERDETERMINED -- the named-father and flesh-seed chain and "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" were both answered, and together they do not settle whether Joseph begat the child.

D6 vs C5 (Galatians 4:4): UNDERDETERMINED -- "made of a woman" was answered as a mortality idiom also used of John, whose father is named, and the words do not state that the woman is the only human source.

D2: STANDS -- no challenger link denies that Joseph was given and performed the naming act; the non-begetter examples deny only that naming alone proves begetting.
D3: STANDS -- the challenger's links do not deny flesh descent from David; they deny only that the text names Joseph as that flesh source.
